stem: A 68-year-old man with rheumatoid arthritis for 15 years fractures his hip in a fall from standing height. Bone density testing shows osteoporosis of the spine and hip. His long-term medications are prednisone, weekly methotrexate, auranofin, hydroxychloroquine and aspirin. Calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels are normal.
oneliner: 68M + RA 15 y + hip fracture after a fall from standing + osteoporosis + takes prednisone, methotrexate, auranofin, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin + normal calcium and vitamin D → which drug?
ask: Which of his medications most likely contributed to his bone loss?

whyNot.A: Main risks are **gastric bleeding and tinnitus**
whyNot.E: At weekly low doses the risks are **marrow, liver and lung**, not bone

why: **Long-term glucocorticoid use** is a leading cause of secondary osteoporosis: **prednisone reduces osteoblast activity, increases osteoclast activity and cuts calcium absorption**.

drug.name: Prednisone
drug.how: Binds the cytosolic receptor and alters gene transcription: less cytokine production and T-cell activity
drug.use: Autoimmune disease, asthma, transplant, adrenal insufficiency
drug.watch: Osteoporosis, avascular necrosis, hyperglycemia, cataracts, infection risk, adrenal suppression

stem: A 52-year-old man had a heart transplant 1 year ago and takes daily maintenance immunosuppression. His blood pressure is now 170/110 mm Hg and his creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 2.1 mg/dL. He has noticed increased facial hair and his gums have thickened. His white cell count is normal and he has no cushingoid features.
oneliner: 52M + heart transplant 1 y ago + BP 170/110 + creatinine 1.1 to 2.1 + more facial hair, thick gums + normal WBC + no cushingoid look → which drug?
ask: Which of the following drugs most likely caused these findings?

whyNot.B: Causes **marrow suppression** and liver injury; his white count is normal
whyNot.C: Can raise blood pressure but he has **no cushingoid features** and it is not directly nephrotoxic
whyNot.D: Causes **hemorrhagic cystitis** and is not a transplant maintenance drug
whyNot.E: Used for **acute rejection** and causes cytokine release, not a long-term hypertension picture

why: **Transplant maintenance drug + hypertension + rising creatinine + hirsutism + gingival overgrowth** = **cyclosporine**. It constricts afferent arterioles, causing **nephrotoxicity and hypertension**.

drug.name: Cyclosporine
drug.how: Binds cyclophilin, inhibits calcineurin, so less IL-2 transcription and T-cell activation
drug.use: Transplant rejection prophylaxis, psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis
drug.watch: Nephrotoxicity, hypertension, hirsutism, gingival hyperplasia, tremor, hyperlipidemia

stem: A 41-year-old woman with Crohn disease has taken infliximab for 6 months. She now has 3 weeks of fever, night sweats and a productive cough with weight loss. Chest x-ray shows a cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe, and sputum smear is positive for acid-fast bacilli. No tuberculosis screening was done before starting therapy.
oneliner: 41F + Crohn disease on infliximab 6 mo + fever, night sweats, productive cough + upper-lobe cavity + AFB-positive sputum → mechanism of reactivation?
ask: Which of the following best explains why this drug predisposed her to this infection?

options.B: Loss of TNF-alpha-dependent macrophage activation and granuloma maintenance
options.C: Reduced antibody production by plasma cells

whyNot.A: Neutrophil recruitment is not what **contains mycobacteria**
whyNot.C: **Antibodies** play a minor role against intracellular organisms
whyNot.D: Not the mechanism of TNF blockade
whyNot.E: She has not yet been treated with **rifampin**

why: **TNF-alpha activates macrophages and holds granulomas together.** **Infliximab** breaks this down, so **latent tuberculosis reactivates**. Screen for TB before TNF blockers.

drug.name: Infliximab
drug.use: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis
drug.watch: Reactivation of latent TB, serious infections, infusion reactions, lymphoma

stem: An 18-year-old man with Crohn disease starts high-dose prednisone. He has no signs of infection. A complete blood count is checked 2 days later.
oneliner: 18M + Crohn disease + started high-dose prednisone + no infection + CBC 2 days later → expected blood-count pattern?
ask: Which blood-count pattern is most likely?

whyNot.A: Every line reversed: with **no infection**, high-dose prednisone **raises** neutrophils and lowers the rest
whyNot.B: Prednisone does not suppress the marrow; **neutrophils rise** within days
whyNot.D: Neutrophils are right, but prednisone **lowers** lymphocytes and eosinophils

why: Glucocorticoids cause **demargination** of neutrophils from vessel walls and reduce their egress into tissue, so the **neutrophil count rises**. **Lymphocytes** and **eosinophils** fall (apoptosis and redistribution).

idea.rule: Steroids raise neutrophils and lower the rest: lymphocytes, eosinophils (and basophils, monocytes).
also: High neutrophil count with no infection after steroids is demargination
Cause adrenal suppression with abrupt withdrawal
Cause cataracts and peptic ulcer with NSAIDs

drug.name: Prednisone
drug.how: Inhibits NF-kB and phospholipase A2; neutrophils leave the marginated pool while lymphocytes and eosinophils fall
drug.use: Crohn disease flares and other inflammatory disease
drug.watch: Neutrophilia with lymphopenia and eosinopenia, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, adrenal suppression

stem: A 46-year-old woman with steroid-resistant kidney transplant rejection receives her first dose of muromonab-CD3 (anti-CD3 antibody). Within hours she has fever, rigors and low blood pressure. She has no hives or wheeze.
oneliner: 46F + steroid-resistant transplant rejection + first dose of muromonab-CD3 (anti-CD3 antibody) + fever, rigors, hypotension within hours + no hives → mechanism?
ask: Which mechanism best explains her reaction?

options.D: Cytokine release from activated T cells

whyNot.A: Would bring **hives and wheeze**; she has neither
whyNot.B: Serum sickness comes **1 to 2 weeks** after a foreign protein, not within hours of the first dose
whyNot.C: Hyperacute rejection occurs **minutes after transplant**; she is already being treated for rejection
whyNot.E: Needs a **bulky tumor** after chemotherapy; she has none

answer: Cytokine release syndrome from T-cell activation after the first dose of muromonab-CD3
why: Anti-CD3 binds the **T-cell receptor complex** and first **activates T cells** before depleting them, releasing **TNF, IL-2 and IFN-gamma**. This produces **fever, rigors and hypotension** with the **first doses**, without urticaria.

idea.rule: First-dose cytokine release: T-cell antibodies activate before they deplete.
also: Antithymocyte globulin can cause the same reaction
Muromonab-CD3 is no longer marketed, but the principle is still tested
Rituximab infusion reactions are similar but milder
CAR-T therapy causes cytokine release syndrome

drug.name: Muromonab-CD3 (OKT3)
drug.how: Binds CD3 on T cells, blocking signaling and depleting T cells
drug.watch: Cytokine release syndrome after the first dose
